rationale: The release job has no explicit timeout, so it falls back to the default 360-minute limit, allowing runaway jobs to consume runner time. Repository CI history shows successful runs complete in about 10 minutes, so representative successful-duration history exists. Applying the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) adds timeout-minutes: 30, roughly 3x the observed successful duration, giving operational headroom while bounding runaway consumption. All existing steps, matrix OS coverage, artifacts, and required checks are preserved; no permissions, secrets, deployment, or network changes are introduced. Yarn dependency caching is already present, so no redundant cache change is made, and fail-fast/stale-run cancellation are unsuitable because every matrix OS artifact is required for a release and this is release/deployment work.
